title: Variable importance
caption: Permutation-importance (mean and standard deviation from 99 permutations, on the x-axis) of the ecogeographical variables (first y-axis, left side), and their variance inflation factor values (second y-axis, right side). **For a full resolution refer to repository: link or online document: link**

title: Marginal responses
caption: Marginalised for arithmetic mean response curves illustrating the effect of each ecogeographical variable on the habitat suitability when all the other variables have their arithmetic mean values. The y-axis shows the predicted habitat suitability (cloglog-transformed), while the x-axis shows the standardised (centred and scaled) value of the ecogeographical variable. Dots at a value of 1 on the y-axis illustrate presence locations in the environment (on the x-axis), while dots at a value of 0 illustrate background locations used in modelling.  **For a full resolution refer to repository: link or online document: link**

title: Habitat and conservation associations
caption: Associations between predicted suitability and: (A) land use land cover classes, (B) Natura 2000 status, (C) stratified EU protected habitat classes, (D) conservation regime, and (E) EU protected habitats. The y-axis show continuous relative suitability index (derivative of Manly's index of preference). Colours in (C) and (E) correspond to stratified EU protected habitat classes. For classifications composed of multiple individual polygons, polygon-level indices were additionally calculated to show within-category variation. The figures therefore combine category-level estimates (points) with the distributions of polygon-level values (boxplots, where applicable). Labels above and below the panels report, respectively, the percentage of total predicted suitability and the percentage of mapped area represented by each category. **For a full resolution refer to repository: link or online document: link**

title: Conservation prioritization
caption: Single-species conservation prioritization focusing on maximisation of core area protection (CAZMAX) while accounting for site connectivity: (A) relative site rank; (B) relationship between apparent-population and extinction-risk curves with a simplified classification which is spatially demonstrated in the bootom row; (C) spatial distribution of proposed classification of site prioritization results. **For a full resolution refer to repository: link or online document: link**
